'''Irwin Ira Shapiro''' is an American [[astrophysicist]] and [[Harvard University Professor|Timken University Professor]] at [[Harvard University]].  He has been a [[professor]] at Harvard since 1982.<ref name="timken">
{{cite news |title=Shapiro Named First Timken University Professor |url=http://www.news.harvard.edu/gazette/1997/10.16/ShapiroNamedFir.html |publisher=Harvard University Gazette |date=1997-10-16 |access-date=2007-02-26 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060902210413/http://www.news.harvard.edu/gazette/1997/10.16/ShapiroNamedFir.html |archive-date=2006-09-02 }}
</ref>  He was the director of the [[Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics|Center for Astrophysics {{!}} Harvard & Smithsonian]] from 1982 to 2004.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://news.harvard.edu/gazette/1998/10.15/Harvard-Smithso.html |title=Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics Celebrates 25 Years |publisher=Harvard University Gazette |date=1998-10-15 |access-date=2007-02-26 |archive-date=2016-04-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160418101542/http://news.harvard.edu/gazette/1998/10.15/Harvard-Smithso.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>
{{cite news |url=http://www.news.harvard.edu/gazette/2004/05.20/01-alcock.html |title=Alcock to lead the CfA |publisher=Harvard University Gazette |date=2004-05-20 |access-date=2007-02-26 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060903100001/http://www.news.harvard.edu/gazette/2004/05.20/01-alcock.html |archive-date=2006-09-03 }}</ref>

==Career==
A native of New York, Shapiro graduated from [[Brooklyn Technical High School]] in New York City.  He later received his [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in [[Mathematics]] from [[Cornell University]], and later a [[Master's degree|M.A.]] and [[Doctorate|Ph.D]] in [[Physics]] from [[Harvard University]].  He joined the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]'s [[Lincoln Laboratory]] in 1954 and became a professor of physics there in 1967. In 1982, he took a position as professor and [[List of Guggenheim Fellowships awarded in 1982|Guggenheim Fellow]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gf.org/fellows/13358-irwin-ira-shapiro |title=Irwin Ira Shapiro - John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation |access-date=2013-02-21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219115424/http://www.gf.org/fellows/13358-irwin-ira-shapiro |archive-date=2013-12-19 }}</ref> at his alma mater, Harvard, and also became director of the [[Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics|Center for Astrophysics {{!}} Harvard & Smithsonian]].  In 1997, he became the first Timken University Professor at the university.<ref name="timken"/>

Shapiro's research interests include [[astrophysics]], [[astrometry]], [[geophysics]], [[gravitation]], including the use of [[gravitational lens]]es to assess the [[age of the universe]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://astronomy.fas.harvard.edu/people/irwin-shapiro |title = Irwin Shapiro}}</ref> In 1981, [[Edward L. G. Bowell|Edward Bowell]] discovered the [[3832 Shapiro|3832]] main belt asteroid and it was later named after Shapiro by his former student [[Steven J. Ostro]].<ref>{{cite book | doi=10.1007/978-3-540-29925-7_3824 | chapter=(3832) Shapiro | title=Dictionary of Minor Planet Names | date=2007 | pages=324–325 | isbn=978-3-540-00238-3 }}</ref>
